### Interface Implementation

### Requirement

Each plugin must implement the appropriate Thunder interfaces.

- PluginHost::IPlugin - Mandatory for all plugins.
- PluginHost::IDispatcher or derive from PluginHost::JSONRPC - Mandatory if the plugin handles JSON-RPC.
- Custom Exchange interfaces must be added to ThunderInterfaces for RPC when the plugin exposes them.
- PluginHost::IWeb - If the plugin handles web requests.

### Example

```cpp
BEGIN_INTERFACE_MAP(AVOutput)
    INTERFACE_ENTRY(PluginHost::IPlugin)
    INTERFACE_ENTRY(PluginHost::IDispatcher)
END_INTERFACE_MAP
```

### Service Registration

### Requirement

All Thunder services must be registered using the SERVICE_REGISTRATION macro with the service name and version numbers (major, minor, patch). Register the service using the following macro:

```
SERVICE_REGISTRATION(ServiceName, MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH)
```

Place this registration in plugin code (typically the main plugin source file) so service name and API version are visible and maintained with the plugin lifecycle code.

For better readability, it is always good to define the following plugin metadata which is not mandatory:

- **Precondition** - List of Thunder subsystems that must be active in order for the plugin to activate. This can also be set in Plugin.conf.in file.

- **Terminations** - List of Thunder subsystems that will cause the plugin to deactivate if they are marked inactive whilst the plugin is running.

- **Controls** - List of the subsystems that are controlled by the plugin.

These metadata arrays are optional but recommended for readability and operational clarity in reviews.

### Example

```cpp
namespace WPEFramework {
    namespace {
        static Plugin::Metadata<Plugin::AVOutput> metadata(
            API_VERSION_NUMBER_MAJOR,
            API_VERSION_NUMBER_MINOR,
            API_VERSION_NUMBER_PATCH,
            {}, // Preconditions
            {}, // Terminations
            {}  // Controls
        );
    }

    namespace Plugin {
        // Register AVOutput service with Thunder
        SERVICE_REGISTRATION(AVOutput, API_VERSION_NUMBER_MAJOR, API_VERSION_NUMBER_MINOR, API_VERSION_NUMBER_PATCH);
    }
}
```

### JSON-RPC Method Registration

### Requirement

AVOutput uses `PluginHost::JSONRPC` through `AVOutputBase`, and the TV implementation registers JSON-RPC methods manually in the `AVOutputTV` constructor using the local `registerMethod` helper.

Keep new AVOutput JSON-RPC handlers registered in the device-type implementation that owns them. Follow the existing constructor-time registration pattern used in `AVOutputTV.cpp`.

### Autogenerated JSON-RPC Stubs

### Requirement

If a plugin uses autogenerated JSON-RPC stubs (`Exchange::J*` classes generated from `interfaces/IPluginName*.h`), register and unregister those stubs in lifecycle methods.

- Register in `Initialize()`.
- Unregister in `Deinitialize()`.
- Do not register/unregister autogenerated stubs in constructor/destructor.

This keeps RPC object lifetime aligned with plugin activation state and avoids stale registrations across activate/deactivate cycles.

### Example

```cpp
const string HdcpProfile::Initialize(PluginHost::IShell* service)
{
    Exchange::JHdcpProfile::Register(*this, _hdcpProfile);
    return string();
}

void HdcpProfile::Deinitialize(PluginHost::IShell* service)
{
    Exchange::JHdcpProfile::Unregister(*this);
}
```

### Example

```cpp
#define registerMethod(...) for (uint8_t i = 1; GetHandler(i); i++) GetHandler(i)->Register<JsonObject, JsonObject>(__VA_ARGS__)

AVOutputTV::AVOutputTV()
    : m_currentHdmiInResoluton(dsVIDEO_PIXELRES_1920x1080)
    , m_videoZoomMode(tvDisplayMode_NORMAL)
    , m_isDisabledHdmiIn4KZoom(false)
    , rfc_caller_id()
{
    InitializeIARM();

    registerMethod("getBacklight", &AVOutputTV::getBacklight, this);
    registerMethod("setZoomMode", &AVOutputTV::setZoomMode, this);
    registerMethod("getVideoFormat", &AVOutputTV::getVideoFormat, this);
}
```

### Lifecycle

### Requirement

Every plugin must implement lifecycle entry points and keep initialization and cleanup deterministic.

- Implement `Initialize(IShell* service)` and `Deinitialize(IShell* service)`.
- Prefer constructor/destructor to stay lightweight. For AVOutput, keep following the established pattern: constructor-time JSON-RPC/IARM setup in `AVOutputTV`, with platform/HAL bring-up in `Initialize()` and platform/HAL teardown in `Deinitialize()`.
- If `Initialize()` acquires resources (callbacks, threads, external handles), `Deinitialize()` and/or destructor must release them in reverse order.

For AVOutput:
- `AVOutput::Initialize()` validates profile support, sets `_skipURL`, then delegates to `DEVICE_TYPE::Initialize()`.
- `AVOutput::Deinitialize()` revalidates profile support and delegates to `DEVICE_TYPE::Deinitialize()`.
- `AVOutputTV::AVOutputTV()` performs JSON-RPC registration, IARM initialization, and worker-thread startup.
- `AVOutputTV::Initialize()` performs TV/HAL setup and callback registration.
- `AVOutputTV::~AVOutputTV()` stops and joins the worker thread and tears down IARM resources.

### Example

```cpp
const string AVOutput::Initialize(PluginHost::IShell* service)
{
    profileType = searchRdkProfile();
    if (profileType == STB || profileType == NOT_FOUND) {
        return std::string("Not supported");
    }

    ASSERT(service != nullptr);
    _skipURL = static_cast<uint8_t>(service->WebPrefix().length());
    DEVICE_TYPE::Initialize();

    return (service != nullptr ? _T("") : _T("No service."));
}

void AVOutput::Deinitialize(PluginHost::IShell* service)
{
    profileType = searchRdkProfile();
    if (profileType == STB || profileType == NOT_FOUND) {
        return;
    }

    DEVICE_TYPE::Deinitialize();
}
```

### Deactivated

### Requirement

Current AVOutput implementation does not define a `Deactivated(...)` method and does not implement `RPC::IRemoteConnection::INotification` in plugin classes.

- Do not add a `Deactivated(...)` path unless the concrete AVOutput code introduces an out-of-process remote connection that requires it.
